```{python}
#| code-fold: show
import copy

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import torch
from torch import nn
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

_ = torch.manual_seed(481)
digits = pd.read_csv("data/optdigits-test.csv", header=None)
x = torch.tensor(digits.iloc[:, :64].to_numpy(), dtype=torch.float32) / 16
y = torch.tensor(digits[64].to_numpy())
n_train, n_val = 150, 400
order = torch.randperm(len(x))
train_idx = order[:n_train]
val_idx = order[n_train:n_train + n_val]
test_idx = order[n_train + n_val:]
x_train, y_train = x[train_idx], y[train_idx]
x_val, y_val = x[val_idx], y[val_idx]
x_test, y_test = x[test_idx], y[test_idx]
n_test = len(x_test)
loss_fn = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()


def make_net(seed=1):
    # 64 pixels, a hidden layer of 256 ReLU units, then 10 logits.
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    return nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(64, 256), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(256, 10))


def accuracy(net, inputs, targets):
    # Share of `inputs` whose largest logit is the true digit.
    net.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        return (net(inputs).argmax(dim=1) == targets).float().mean().item()


def fit(net, n_epochs=300, weight_decay=0.0, transform=None, seed=0):
    # Full-batch AdamW on the training images.
    # Records both losses after every epoch, and keeps the parameters
    # from the epoch with the lowest validation loss.
    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(net.parameters(), lr=0.01, weight_decay=weight_decay)
    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    history, best_state, best_val = [], None, float("inf")
    for epoch in range(1, n_epochs + 1):
        net.train()
        inputs = x_train if transform is None else transform(x_train, generator)
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss_fn(net(inputs), y_train).backward()
        optimizer.step()
        net.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            train_loss = loss_fn(net(x_train), y_train).item()
            val_loss = loss_fn(net(x_val), y_val).item()
        history.append({"epoch": epoch, "train": train_loss, "val": val_loss})
        if val_loss < best_val:
            best_val, best_state = val_loss, copy.deepcopy(net.state_dict())
    return pd.DataFrame(history), best_state


n_params = sum(p.numel() for p in make_net().parameters())
print(len(x_train), len(x_val), len(x_test), n_params)
```

The exercises use the `r format(nrow(py$digits), big.mark = ",")` digits of [`data/optdigits-test.csv`](data/optdigits-test.csv) [@alpaydin1998optdigits].
To make a network fit its training images too well,
the [training set](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-training-set) here is small,
`r py$n_train` random images.
Another `r py$n_val` form a [validation set](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-validation-set),
and the other `r format(py$n_test, big.mark = ",")` a [test set](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-test-set).
`make_net()` builds an [MLP](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-feedforward-network) with one [hidden layer](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-hidden-layer) of 256 [ReLU](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-relu) [units](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-unit),
which has `r format(py$n_params, big.mark = ",")` [parameters](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-parameter).
`fit()` trains it by full-batch AdamW,
PyTorch's variant of [Adam](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-adam) with weight decay,
with [learning rate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-learning-rate) 0.01 and no weight decay unless asked.
It records the training and validation losses after every [epoch](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-epoch).
